findings.text: Device query service enumerates host supported or emulated processor identification leaves into caller storage. It rejects empty requests, clamps oversized counts, validates padding for emulated queries, allocates temporary kernel storage, walks four base families in fixed order, updates the count to what was produced, and copies results to user space.

Guest instruction emulation entry for processor identification first checks guest permission and raises a protection fault on denial. On allowance it takes requested function and index from guest registers, performs a non exact lookup that may fall back to the maximum basic leaf, writes back four result registers, and advances past the emulated instruction.

Public lookup routine resolves an identification request for a virtual processor given function and index values. It refreshes dynamic feature bits when marked dirty, prefers an exact match, optionally redirects out of range requests to the maximum basic entry, applies runtime adjustments for transactional memory reporting and Hyper-V invariant timestamp suppression, zeroes missing leaves with special handling for topology leaves, records a trace event, and reports whether the match was exact.
Public register read helper forwards to an internal getter with host initiated context enabled, returning the backend status and filling the output value only on success.
Public accessor reports the effective maximum two dimensional paging level, preferring an explicitly configured root level when nonzero and otherwise returning the default maximum.

Leaf construction for low basic functions caps the maximum basic identifier, replaces feature words from a central capability table, warns if the historic stateful descriptor leaf indicates repeated queries, expands deterministic cache leaves until an invalid cache type appears, returns a fixed thermal report that only advertises automatic rate adjustment, and limits the structured feature leaf to two subleaves with selective capability replacement and zeroing of remaining registers.

Monitoring, topology and extended state leaves are sanitized: monitoring is zeroed unless both the global enable and host support hold, otherwise filled from a capability record with version dependent deprecation; topology leaves are cleared to indicate no topology; extended state masks permitted components, derives save sizes, conditionally includes supervisor components, walks possible subleaves, discards entries with zero size or mismatched supervisor flag, and clears a disable bit when the host lacks the corresponding capability.

Enclave, tracing, matrix and vector extension leaves plus hypervisor signature leaves follow gated enumeration: each hardware gated leaf is zeroed when its host capability is absent, otherwise subleaves are copied from the host with bounded maxima and capability masking, enclave attribute masks distinguish privileged and unprivileged bits, matrix tile and transpose leaves share one gate, vector version is clamped before feature masking, and signature leaves publish a fixed signature with a defined set of paravirtual feature bits plus conditional steal time.

Extended and Centaur leaves enforce upper bounds and masking: the maximum extended identifier is clamped with an adjustment that promotes a newer leaf when serializing fence or fixed null segment behavior is present and the cache topology leaf exists, feature words are replaced from central caps while clearing reserved ranges, power and address size leaves are masked against host values with distinct handling for shadow versus two dimensional paging widths, virtualization and security leaves are zeroed or fixed when unsupported, topology is suppressed, and unknown functions including serial, monitor and unspecified Centaur leaves are fully zeroed.

Override helper selects one 32 bit register inside an entry using a compact leaf identifier scaled to bit position and replaces its entire contents with the corresponding value from the global host capability table, with a build time check that the identifier stays within the table.

Filtered extended control helper starts from the globally supported mask, intersects dynamically managed tile bits with the current process group permission when any such bit is present, and additionally drops the tile configuration bit when tile data permission is absent because the former cannot be valid alone; it also asserts at build time that two tile masks coincide.

Function dispatcher chooses emulated versus standard construction based on query type. The range expander skips the Centaur base on other vendors, builds the requested function, then sequentially builds following functions up to the maximum identifier reported by the last produced entry, stopping early on error.
Padding validator only applies to emulated queries and reports failure if user padding cannot be read or contains any nonzero word; all other query types bypass the check.

Out of range resolver returns no entry for missing basic leaf or for guests identifying as two specific vendors. Otherwise it selects a class entry by masking hypervisor, Centaur, or standard versus extended ranges, returns no entry when the request falls within the class maximum, and otherwise redirects the request to the maximum basic leaf while preserving the original index.

When no entry exists the lookup zeroes all outputs, except topology functions where it propagates the low byte of the index and reuses the identifier from subleaf one when that subleaf exists. When an entry exists for structured features it may clear transactional memory bits based on a control register value, and for advanced power management it may clear the invariant timestamp bit under Hyper-V suppression.

Internal register getter enforces guest capability gates before delegating to the architecture backend: timestamp auxiliary requires host support plus guest capability for guest initiated reads, control flow enforcement registers require shadow stack or branch tracking, shadow stack range requires shadow stack, and an internal guest stack pointer is host only and shares the shadow stack gate.

Two builds of the invariant timestamp suppression predicate exist: one always reports no suppression, while the other reports suppression only when per processor Hyper-V feature cache exposes invariant timestamp access and the per machine control does not enable exposure. A tiny accessor returns the Hyper-V state embedded in the virtual machine structure.

Host capability queries for one function execute pinned to the current processor with preemption disabled to keep repeated reads consistent, releasing the pin on all exit paths including capacity failures.

Array container observed in use carries a current entry count, a maximum capacity, and a pointer to a contiguous entry buffer. Each entry carries at least function, index and four output words plus padding observed in user validation, with the last entry maximum field used to bound sequential expansion.

Enumeration proceeds through validation, capacity clamping, temporary allocation, ordered expansion over four base families with inner sequential expansion to each family maximum, count update, user copy, and cleanup. Errors at expansion abort further families but still release the buffer; copy failure is reported after the count update.

Extended state enumeration starts at subleaf zero, requires a nonzero permitted mask to continue, processes subleaf one with size derivation dependent on save feature presence, then scans higher component identifiers and skips unsupported bits, queries the host for each permitted bit, validates size and supervisor flag agreement, and either drops or finalizes the entry before continuing.

Capacity exhaustion during entry insertion, temporary allocation failure, unreadable or nonzero padding on emulated queries, and user copy failure each produce distinct negative error codes without partial user visible counts except the final copy stage which updates the count before reporting the fault.

One shot warnings guard against unexpected host behavior: a stateful descriptor count above one, nonzero supervisor state without save support, and a host subleaf that reports zero size or disagrees on supervisor management, the last case causing the freshly added entry to be removed and enumeration to continue.
Centaur base leaf identifier equals 0xC0000000.

Implementation caps observed: basic maximum clamped to 0x24, structured feature maximum clamped to 2, transpose maximum clamped to 1, vector maximum clamped to 1 with version clamped to 2, extended maximum clamped to 0x80000022, Centaur maximum clamped to 0xC0000004, and virtual address width promoted to at least 48.
